To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) research and evaluation methods are not value free, (b) the culture of research must be changed to include American Indians and Alaska Native peoples, and (c) American Indians and Alaska natives are the only people who can determine what research and evaluation methods to use.

(1) research with Native people should be conducted in a collaborative manner, with the community as a partner; (2) research with Native peoples should be conducted in an ethical manner, with the protection of the community as a primary goal; (3) the research design should be based on the needs of the community; (4) research with Native communities should include the use of qualitative and quantitative methods; and (5) research should be culturally relevant and culturally sensitive.

(a) research and program evaluation with Native peoples is best conducted by Native researchers, in collaboration with other researchers and practitioners; (b) the research process should be culturally based and community driven; (c) the research process must include community input at all stages; and (d) research findings must be disseminated to all parties involved.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a research agenda and a set of research and evaluation methods that reflect the cultural and political realities of American Indians and Alaskan Natives.
the development of culturally appropriate research and evaluation methodologies for American Indians and Alaska natives, with a particular emphasis on the therapeutic residential model.
the need to develop a research agenda that will address the issues of American Indian and Alaska Native communities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

research and evaluation methods that are culturally appropriate and sensitive, and that respect the values and traditions of Native peoples, are necessary to understand the needs, strengths, and challenges facing Native communities today.
research and evaluation methods must be developed in collaboration with the communities being served and that these methods must be culturally appropriate.

the American Indian Research and Evaluation Methodology Project was a success in terms of the following: (1) the establishment of a national network of Native American researchers; (2) the creation of a national research and evaluation methodology symposium; (3) the development of the 20 guiding principles; (4) the creation of an ongoing national network of Native research and evaluation professionals; and (5) the development of a national research agenda for Native American research and program evaluation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are working to develop research methods that are respectful, culturally appropriate, and that are grounded in Native values and world views.
the research community needs to be more responsive to the needs of American Indian and Alaska Native people.
research is a tool for social change, and that research and evaluation should be used to empower and support Native communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
research with American Indian and Alaska Native populations must be conducted with a deep respect for culture and community.
research and program evaluation with American Indians and Alaska Native peoples requires the use of culturally appropriate methodologies.
research and program evaluation methods must reflect the values, traditions, and culture of the community being studied.
